import pandas as pd

def main():
    # Source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_21/test_0.csv"
    ]

    # List to hold dataframes from all sources
    dfs = []

    # Load each source file, transform and append to dfs
    for file_path in source_files:
        df = pd.read_csv(file_path)

        # We only need 'Major_category' and 'Median' columns
        # Group by 'Major_category' and calculate the mean of 'Median'
        # Median column might have missing values, so mean will ignore NaNs by default
        grouped = df.groupby('Major_category', as_index=False)['Median'].mean()

        dfs.append(grouped)

    # Concatenate all grouped dataframes (if multiple sources)
    combined = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # Since multiple sources might have overlapping Major_category,
    # group again to get the final mean Median per Major_category
    final_df = combined.groupby('Major_category', as_index=False)['Median'].mean()

    # Sort by Major_category alphabetically (optional, for neatness)
    final_df = final_df.sort_values('Major_category').reset_index(drop=True)

    # Write the final dataframe to the target CSV file
    final_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_21/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
